title: Choose the look for muzamilkhanrealtor.com
question: The roll picked 'The Spec Sheet'. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll for a new hand.

options.label: The Spec Sheet
options.lineage: MLS listing data sheets and your one-page playbooks
options.thesis: Every page reads like a listing spec sheet: the real numbers first, then your plain-English read.
options.viewport: Your photo beside a market strip for your four cities (median, % over asking) and one big 'Text me' action.
options.risk: Can feel like a dashboard if your photos and voice do not lead.

raised.raise: Each city owns one color, carried from its site page to its playbook and IG posts, so people find their city by color.
Buying runs as fixed numbered stations in order, the same rail on Buy, the playbooks, and the blog's Start here.

options.label: The Inspection Report
options.lineage: home inspection reports and construction drawings
options.thesis: The site annotated like an inspection report: what the house is, what it needs, what it costs.
options.viewport: A house drawing with numbered callouts beside 'I read the house, not just the listing.'
options.risk: The 'blueprint' look is familiar and can feel technical to first-time buyers.

options.label: Tabbed Reference Manual
options.lineage: boxed-software manuals with colored divider tabs
options.thesis: The site as a tabbed manual: one colored tab per section down the edge.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail with Buy, Sell, Neighborhoods, Blog as colored tabs.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the manual metaphor adds weight to a site that needs to feel simple.
options.kept: One color per section for wayfinding.
options.risk: Busy and retro if the tabs dominate.

options.label: Darkroom Stations
options.thesis: Work moves through fixed stations in a set order.
options.viewport: Amber-lit stations for each step of buying.
options.case: Fuses poorly: buyers do not identify with a darkroom; amber hurts readability.
options.kept: Steps run in a fixed, numbered order.
options.risk: Dark and moody, the opposite of simple.

options.label: East Bay at Night
options.lineage: blue-hour cityscape, transit lights, wet streets
options.thesis: The Bay at blue hour, with BART lines as the paths between cities.
options.viewport: A night skyline with amber transit lines linking your four cities.
options.case: Fuses partly: local and atmospheric, but dark and heavy, which you already moved away from.
options.kept: Cities connected as one map you move along.
options.risk: Reads like the old dark site.

options.label: Spectrum Rail
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one rail; color only as thin lines.
options.viewport: A dark rail with each page as a tick mark.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too abstract and technical for buyers.

options.label: Memory Quilt
options.thesis: Each block a different story, stitched together.
options.case: Fuses poorly: crafty and busy, not modern.
options.kept: Every story keeps its source visible.

options.label: Album-Sleeve Collage
options.thesis: Cut-out photos pasted at wild scales.
options.viewport: Your photo cut out in a painted scene.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful but undermines trust for a big purchase.

canonCard.label: The standard realtor site
canonCard.thesis: What top agent sites ship (Compass-style), executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Big photo of you, your cities as photo tiles, reviews, and contact.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other agent site by design.
